title: The Jar of Almost-Names
content: Four chronological movements record Lexor's arrival, the next morning and day, Privathor's third-morning departure and voluntary return, and the fourth day. On the fourth day, Brograntimax repairs the stove-side chair without his measuring chain; it is available to anyone and reserved for nobody. The fourth-day scene is written in Portuguese with an Aramaic literary parallel in Hebrew square script. The jar's function and Lexor's withdrawn name remain unresolved.
continuity: The chapter preserves four successive movements. Privathor remains free to leave and return; the chair is maintained but not reserved. The jar's function, the name Lexor tried to withdraw, and any meaning of the pebble's small movement remain unknown.
